idiom_name: hand-staged change set flushed with upsert_all inside a transaction
implementation_notes: Active Record saves per object - create/save/update hit the database immediately - so there is no persistence context that defers writes, and the pattern must be built. Collect staged rows in a registry keyed by id, and at the commit boundary flush the registry with upsert_all (or insert_all for pure inserts), which emits a single multi-row INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE statement inside the surrounding transaction. What replaces the classic structure: only the bulk write API is provided; per-object dirty tracking (changed_attributes) is consumed by each save and cannot coalesce across objects.
pitfalls: upsert_all skips validations and callbacks, so anything that must gate persistence belongs before staging.
Clearing the registry before the transaction commits loses writes on rollback - clear only after commit.
The registry is process memory: a crash between stage and flush loses the changes unless they are logged or outboxed first.
